text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Russia is ready to grant Bulgaria some 150,000 tonnes of wheat, Russia's ambassador to Sofia said in the northern town of Pleven.
-- Bulgaria's caretaker government is expected to finalise its economic reform programme and present it to the International Monetary Fund mission by the end of its stay in Sofia. @

-- Some 94 percent of foreign investments in Bulgaria were below $50,000 last year, which prevented investors from taking advantage of tax benefits under the country's Foreign Investment Law, Foreign Investment Agency figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's Socialist Party is expected to win some 20 to 25 percent of the vote in the country's early general elections on April 19, former Socialist prime minister Zhan Videnov said.
-- A portion of excise duties on fuel and car imports should be allocated for repairs of the Bulgaria's roads and highways, a draft by transport ministry experts said. @

-- Bulgarians have withrawn more than 20 billion levs from their savings in local commercial banks at the end of January and the beginning of February as prices of basic goods soared, central bank statistics show.

-- The first shipment out of a total of 100,000 tonnes of Polish wheat, negotiated by Bulgaria's President Petar Stoyanov during his recent visit to Warsaw, are expected to arrive in Bulgaria by the end of the week, said Bulgarian State Railways head Yordan Michev. @

-- The executive bureau of the Bulgarian Socialist Party is expected to discuss today the Socialists' two-year performance in office and to pinpoint the culprits for the country's grave economic crisis.
-- France would support Bulgaria's bid for a rescheduling of Sofia's debt to the Paris Club of government creditors, Interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said on return from a visit to Paris.

-- A trader in weapons and non-ferrous metals was shot dead and his wife and four-year old daughter were slaughtered in their home in Sofia late on Sunday for yet unknown reasons, the interior ministry said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
